requirements.note: Inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, sorted newest first. Each row shows the title and then a date line (time / Yesterday / weekday / short date) followed by a one-line preview.
Search field in the nav bar under the large title filters title and body live, shows an 'N Results' count and a proper 'No Results for …' empty state.
Editor has a multiline title and body that autosave. The edited note jumped to the top of Notes with today's time and the scroll position was kept. Shows a Done checkmark while editing.
Compose button opens a new note with the keyboard up. Backing out of an empty note leaves the count at 90, and a note with text is kept (91).
Swipe left gives Delete, a full swipe right pins, and long-press opens a context menu with Pin/Unpin Note and Delete. All of these persisted.
'90 Notes' in the bottom toolbar, as in Apple Notes. It updates on create and delete and becomes 'N Results' while searching.
Edits, new notes, pins, unpins and deletes all survived a relaunch.

tells: At the largest text size the editor breaks a long word mid-word ('recommendat/ions') in the title and body. This is plain text-view wrapping, but it still breaks inside a word.
At the largest text size the '90 Notes' toolbar count does not grow with Dynamic Type, and row previews wrap to two lines on some rows but not others.
When scrolled, the floating search field sits over the list content and the text underneath shows through a little busily.
A.scroll: Feels like a real UITableView: slow drags track the finger, flings decelerate naturally with no blank or popping rows, and it rubber-bands at the top. Scroll position is kept when coming back from the editor.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first, with title, a relative/short date and a one-line preview. Long titles wrap to two lines.
Bottom search field (iOS 26 toolbar style) filters title and body as you type, with a 'No Results' empty state. It shows no result count.
Body edits autosave and the note moves to the top of Notes with today's time. The date header reads 'Today at …'.
Compose opens a new note with the keyboard up. An empty note is discarded and a note with text is kept.

Swipe left gives Delete, and long-press opens a context menu with Pin/Unpin Note and Delete. There is no leading swipe to pin: a rightward drag on a row opened the note instead. All changes persisted.
'90 Notes' appears as a subtitle under the large title and in the inline title, and it updates. It is hidden while searching.
Edits, new notes, pins, unpins and deletes all survived a relaunch.

bugs: A rightward swipe on a row opens the note instead of offering a pin action. (One earlier tap on a row near the bottom search bar also did nothing.)
tells: The title in the editor is a single-line text field: at the largest text size a long title truncates to 'Ideas for the…' and the user cannot see the whole title while editing it.
No Done button to dismiss the keyboard while editing.
The 'No Results' empty-state title is regular weight rather than the bold system ContentUnavailableView title.
At the largest text size the editor breaks a long word mid-word ('recommendatio/ns'), the same as A.
Each list row is exposed as one big Button inside a cell rather than as a normal table cell, and the nav bar exposes an odd 'ExactKit.Route' identifier. Only VoiceOver users would notice either.
B.scroll: Smooth and native-feeling: drags track the finger, flings decelerate with no blank or popping rows, there is top rubber-banding, and position is kept after editing. Rows are slightly taller than A's.

why: Both apps meet nearly every requirement and scroll like native lists. A is a closer match to Apple Notes: it pins with a swipe as well as from the long-press menu, has a multiline title, a Done button and a result count. B has no swipe-to-pin, its single-line title truncates at large text, and a few details (the empty-state weight, no Done button) are slightly off.
